examples.en: After graduating from university, he started farming.
There is a program that supports successors to family farms.
I took out a loan for the funds needed for farming.

examples.ko: 영농은 날씨에 따라 수확이 크게 달라져요.
examples.en: In farming, the harvest changes a lot depending on the weather.
Farmers gathered to learn new farming methods.
She paid for her children's education with money earned from farming.

explain: 일상에서 농사짓는 일은 보통 '농사'라고 해요. 영농은 '영농 조합', '영농 후계자', '영농 자금'처럼 제도나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그는 아버지를 이어 영농 후계자가 됐어요.
phrases.en: He became a successor farmer, following his father.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농사일을 이어받을 사람을 가리키는 제도 속 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A term from farming policy for the person who will carry on the farm.

phrases.en: The villagers formed a farming cooperative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농부들이 함께 농사를 짓거나 판매하는 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group where farmers farm or sell together.

phrases.en: My grandfather farmed all his life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 농사짓는 일을 말할 때는 '영농'보다 '농사'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, use 농사 rather than 영농 for the work of farming.

explain_en: Running a farm as a business — formal, written. In daily life, working the land is usually called '농사'. 영농 appears in institutional or news contexts, such as '영농 조합', '영농 후계자' and '영농 자금'.

t90.ax: Farmers gathered to learn new farming methods.

en: to bring something to match something else

examples.en: Please make the dates in the two documents match.
I try to make my words and actions match.
It's hard to line up everyone's schedules.
It looks much neater now that the colors match.
We played a game of matching photos with names.
We present after aligning our opinions.

explain: 사람이 일부러 두 가지를 서로 맞게 할 때 써요. 저절로 맞는 것은 '일치하다', 맞춰진 상태는 '일치되다', 맞추는 행동은 '일치시키다'예요. 일상에서는 '맞추다'가 더 쉽고 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Please match up the times with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일치시키다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 훨씬 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '일치시키다' and used much more in daily life.

phrases.en: Please make the numbers in the two tables match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 일부러 맞춰 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask someone to make two things match.

phrases.en: I couldn't make my words and actions match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞추려고 했지만 잘 안 된 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you tried to make things match but couldn't.

explain_en: Used when a person deliberately makes two things fit. '일치하다' matches by itself, '일치되다' is the matched state, and '일치시키다' is the act of matching. In daily speech '맞추다' is easier and more common.

examples.en: All the materials in the library have been digitized.

examples.ko: 병원 기록의 전산화는 몇 년 전에 끝났어요.
examples.en: The digitization of hospital records was finished a few years ago.
The company started digitizing its documents.
Thanks to digitization, it has become easy to find documents.

examples.ko: 시청은 민원 업무 전산화에 힘쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: The city hall is working hard on digitizing its civil service work.
Digitization is late, so we still accept applications on paper.

explain: '전산'은 회사나 관공서에서 '전산 시스템', '전산 오류'처럼 컴퓨터로 처리하는 일을 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 그래서 '전산화'는 종이로 하던 일을 컴퓨터로 옮기는 업무 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: We are starting the digitization work this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전산화'만 말할 때보다 실제로 하는 일을 가리켜서 업무 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It points to the actual work of digitizing, so it is common when talking about office tasks.

phrases.en: Our school finished digitization last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전산화가 다 이루어졌다는 뜻으로, 일이 마무리된 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the digitization is fully done, used when the job is finished.

phrases.example: 이 병원은 모든 기록이 전산화되어 있어요.
phrases.en: At this hospital, all records are digitized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 상태가 이미 컴퓨터로 처리된다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the current state of already being handled by computer.

explain_en: '전산' is used in offices and public institutions in phrases like '전산 시스템' (computer system) and '전산 오류' (system error). So '전산화' often comes up when talking about moving work from paper to computers.

en: garbage man; sanitary worker; street cleaner

examples.en: The street cleaner sweeps the road from dawn.
The building cleaner is mopping the hallway.
Thanks to the cleaners, the streets are clean.

examples.ko: 청소부께 아침마다 인사를 하면 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Greeting the cleaner every morning makes me feel good.
My friend's father works as a cleaner.
A cleaner's work is hard but absolutely necessary.

explain: 공식 글이나 뉴스에서는 거리 청소하는 사람을 '환경미화원'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '아저씨', '아주머니'가 자연스러워요. 청소부는 일을 낮춰 보는 느낌으로 들릴 수 있어서 조심해서 써요.

phrases.en: Sanitation workers clean the streets at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 공식 글에서 쓰는 더 공손한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more respectful term used in news and formal writing.

phrases.en: I greeted the cleaning lady.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 만나서 부르거나 말할 때 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer when speaking to or about the person directly.

phrases.en: My father works as a cleaner at a school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 설명할 때 쓰지만 조심해서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a job, but use it carefully.

explain_en: In formal writing and news, people who clean the streets are called '환경미화원'. When addressing one directly, '아저씨' or '아주머니' sounds natural. 청소부 can sound as if it looks down on the job, so use it carefully.

t90.ax: My friend's father works as a cleaner.

en: to eliminate; to fail; to knock out

examples.ko: 심사위원이 첫 라운드에서 세 팀을 탈락시켰어요.
examples.en: The judges eliminated three teams in the first round.
The company did not eliminate any applicants at the interview.

examples.ko: 실수 하나 때문에 저를 탈락시키다니 너무해요.
examples.en: Eliminating me over a single mistake is too harsh.

examples.ko: 감독이 선수 두 명을 대표팀에서 탈락시킬 거예요.
examples.en: The coach is going to cut two players from the national team.

examples.ko: 약한 팀을 탈락시키고 다음 경기를 시작했어요.
examples.en: They knocked out the weaker teams and started the next match.
Audition programs that eliminate people are nerve-racking.

explain: '떨어지다'는 시험이나 경쟁에서 내가 떨어질 때, '탈락시키다'는 심사하는 쪽이 다른 사람을 떨어뜨릴 때 써요. 당하는 사람 쪽에서는 '탈락하다', '탈락되다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The interviewer rejected the applicant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말이에요. '탈락시키다'는 더 공식적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word; 탈락시키다 is more formal.

phrases.en: Our team was eliminated in the first round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨어지는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person who is eliminated is the subject.

phrases.en: The score is low, so we have no choice but to eliminate them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심사하는 쪽이 어쩔 수 없이 결정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the judging side has no choice but to decide this.
phrases.en_equiv: have no choice but to eliminate

explain_en: Transitive: judges drop a team or person (점수가 낮은 팀을 탈락시키다) '떨어지다' is what you say when you fail a test or competition yourself; '탈락시키다' is used by the side doing the judging, who knocks someone out. From the point of view of the person eliminated, you say '탈락하다' or '탈락되다'.

examples.en: The factory runs its machines every morning.
They started running the new power plant yesterday.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 난방 시설을 가동하는 시간이 길어요.
examples.en: In winter, the heating system runs for a longer time.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 배수 펌프를 가동할 거예요.
examples.en: If it rains a lot, they'll turn on the drainage pump.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터 서버를 하루 종일 가동하고 있어요.
examples.en: We keep the computer server running all day.

examples.ko: 비상 상황에는 이 장치를 바로 가동해야 해요.
examples.en: In an emergency, you have to start this device right away.

explain: 큰 기계나 설비, 시스템을 움직이게 하거나 계속 돌릴 때 써요. 집에서 쓰는 가전은 '켜다'나 '틀다'가 자연스러워요. 반대는 '중단하다'나 '멈추다'예요.

phrases.en: This factory runs its machines 24 hours a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬지 않고 계속 돌릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for running something nonstop.

phrases.en: The new system began operating today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 움직이기 시작했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something has started running.

phrases.en: The factory stopped operating because of an accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아가던 것을 멈출 때 쓰는 반대 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite expression, for stopping operation.

explain_en: Used for starting or keeping large machines, facilities or systems running. For home appliances, 켜다 or 틀다 sounds more natural. The opposite is 중단하다 or 멈추다.

dis.h: start up and run machinery or a factory
gh: a device works or functions properly

p.n: 작동하다 does not take 'machine' as an object.

t90.ax: The factory runs its machines every morning.

examples.en: Exercise reduces stress.
The company is trying to reduce costs.

examples.ko: 이 약은 통증을 감소시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can reduce pain.
I'm looking for ways to cut down on trash.
The new system greatly reduced accidents.
After reducing the noise, it became much quieter.

explain: '줄이다'와 같지만, 줄어드는 대상이 양·수치·비율처럼 측정되는 것일 때 글이나 보고서에서 많이 써요. 스스로 줄어들면 '감소하다'이고, 누군가가 줄게 만들면 '감소시키다'예요. 말할 때는 '줄이다'가 훨씬 흔해요.

phrases.en: The number of customers decreased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 한 것이 아니라 저절로 줄어드는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something decreases by itself, with no agent.

phrases.example: 비용을 줄이면 돈을 아낄 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you cut costs, you can save money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감소시키다'보다 말할 때 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word used much more in speech than 감소시키다.

phrases.example: 이 약은 통증 감소 효과가 있어요.
phrases.en: This medicine has an effect of reducing pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 줄어드는 효과를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe an effect of making something decrease.

explain_en: Deliberately reduce levels or amounts — formal. Same idea as '줄이다', but typical in reports and writing when the thing reduced is a measurable amount or rate. '감소하다' is when something decreases by itself; '감소시키다' is when someone makes it decrease. In speech, '줄이다' is far more common.

dis.h: formal; make amounts or levels drop

p.n: 줄이다 is everyday speech; 감소시키다 is more formal or technical.

examples.en: Please don't think of the two matters as linked.
Why do you tie every problem to age?

examples.ko: 그는 성공을 운과 결부시키는 걸 싫어해요.
examples.en: He dislikes attributing success to luck.

examples.ko: 그 일을 제 실수와 결부시킬 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to link that matter to my mistake.

examples.ko: 성적을 용돈과 결부시켰더니 아이가 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: After I tied grades to allowance, the child studied hard.
If you force a link between the incidents, misunderstandings arise.

explain: 'A를 B와 결부시키다'처럼 말하는 사람이 둘을 엮어서 본다는 뜻이에요. '결부시키지 마세요'나 '억지로 결부시키다'처럼 쓰면 무리하게 엮는다는 느낌이 있어요. 스스로 연결되어 있는 경우는 '결부되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Don't think of success only in connection with money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결부시키다'에 '생각하다'를 이어, 둘을 하나로 묶어서 생각한다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '생각하다' to '결부시키다' makes it clear you are linking two things together in your mind.

phrases.example: 두 사건을 억지로 결부시키는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It seems like you're forcing a link between the two incidents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억지로'를 붙이면 무리하게 엮는다는 비판의 느낌이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: '억지로' makes the criticism of forcing a connection clear.

phrases.example: 모든 일을 한 가지 이유와 엮어서 생각하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't link everything to a single reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결부시키다'보다 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say '결부시키다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to link together in one's mind

explain_en: It means the speaker ties two things together, as in 'A를 B와 결부시키다'. In phrases like '결부시키지 마세요' or '억지로 결부시키다' it carries a sense of forcing a link. When the link exists on its own, use '결부되다'.

dis.h: formal: tie A firmly to B
gh: make a link: associate A with B

p.n: 연관시키다 is plainer and less formal.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들은 대부분 쌀 경작으로 먹고살아요.
examples.en: Most people in this village make a living from rice cultivation.
The cultivated area is shrinking every year.
Cultivation is not easy on a mountain slope.
Grandfather hurt his back from long years of farming.
Farmland is disappearing little by little near the city.

examples.ko: 경작에 쓰는 땅은 비가 충분히 와야 좋아요.
examples.en: Land used for cultivation needs enough rain to be good.

explain: 일상에서는 '농사'라고 많이 말하고, 경작은 뉴스나 설명문에서 땅을 일구는 일을 말할 때 나와요. '경작지', '경작 면적'처럼 땅과 함께 쓰는 말이 많아요. '농사'가 일 전체라면 경작은 땅에 초점이 있어요.

phrases.en: This area has a lot of farmland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농사를 짓는 땅을 가리키는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to land used for farming.

phrases.en: It's a village that farms on the mountain slopes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 땅을 일구는 일을 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '하다' says someone works the land.

phrases.en: This land is suitable for cultivation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅의 조건을 설명할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for describing land conditions.

explain_en: Growing crops on a field (밭 경작); agricultural. In daily talk people say '농사' (farming), while 경작 appears in news and written explanations about working the land. It often forms words tied to land, like '경작지' and '경작 면적'. '농사' is the whole job, while 경작 focuses on the land.

t90.ax: The cultivated area is shrinking every year.

examples.ko: 선생님은 새 단어를 일상생활과 관련시켜 가르쳐 주세요.
examples.en: The teacher teaches new words by relating them to daily life.

examples.ko: 이 사건을 그 사람과 관련시키지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't connect this incident to that person.
I thought about the two things together.
If you link a memory to a place, it lasts longer.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일을 제 문제와 관련시켰어요.
examples.en: I connected that matter to my own problem.
The news is linking the two incidents.

explain: '관련되다'는 저절로 연결된 상태이고, '관련시키다'는 누군가 일부러 연결한다는 차이가 있어요. '연결하다'는 물건이나 선에도 쓰지만 '관련시키다'는 일이나 생각을 이을 때 써요. '~을 ~와 관련시키다' 틀로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 노래를 옛 추억과 관련시켜 생각해요.
phrases.en: I connect this song with old memories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 이어서 생각할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you link two things in your thinking.
phrases.en_equiv: to think of in connection with

phrases.en: I memorize new words by linking them to pictures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부 방법을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when describing study methods.

phrases.en: Can you link the two events?
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결할 수 있는지 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask whether things can be connected.

explain_en: Transitive — you link one thing to another (실생활과 관련시키다) '관련되다' is a state of being linked on its own, while '관련시키다' means someone links things on purpose. '연결하다' also works for objects and lines, but '관련시키다' is used for events and ideas. The pattern is '~을 ~와 관련시키다'.

gh: see or treat two things as linked

p.n: Nearly the same; 관련짓다 stresses seeing a link in the mind.

examples.en: The baby lies there wiggling its fingers.

examples.ko: 아이는 방 한구석에서 꼼지락꼼지락 뭔가를 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child was making something slowly in a corner of the room.
I watched TV, wiggling my toes.

examples.ko: 새끼 고양이가 담요 속에서 꼼지락꼼지락 기어 나왔어요.
examples.en: The kitten wriggled its way out of the blanket.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 하루 종일 꼼지락꼼지락 화분을 손질하세요.
examples.en: Grandpa spends all day slowly tending to his flower pots.

examples.ko: 동생이 꼼지락꼼지락 딴짓만 해서 숙제를 못 끝냈어요.
examples.en: My sibling kept fiddling around and couldn't finish the homework.

explain: '꼼지락거리다'의 부사로, 손가락·발가락처럼 몸의 일부가 느리고 조금씩 움직이는 모습이에요. 작은 동물이나 벌레가 기어가는 느낌은 '꼬물꼬물'이 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The baby is wiggling its toes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼼지락꼼지락'의 동사형이에요. 문장 끝에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 꼼지락꼼지락, which can end a sentence.

phrases.en: The little wiggling hands are so cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe how it looks.

phrases.en: The child keeps fidgeting in the seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼼지락거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 꼼지락거리다 and comfortable in casual speech.

explain_en: It is the adverb of '꼼지락거리다', describing a part of the body such as fingers or toes moving slowly and slightly. For the feel of a small animal or bug crawling, '꼬물꼬물' fits better.

en: (unable to) budge at all; not moving an inch

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 사람으로 꽉 차서 꼼짝달싹 못 했어요.
examples.en: The elevator was packed, so I couldn't move an inch.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 도로의 차들이 꼼짝달싹 못 해요.
examples.en: Because of the heavy snow, the cars on the road can't budge.

examples.ko: 감기가 심해서 하루 종일 꼼짝달싹 안 하고 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I had a bad cold, so I lay there all day without moving.

examples.ko: 허리를 다쳐서 꼼짝달싹 할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my back and can't move at all.
Mom is watching me, so I can't make a single move.

examples.ko: 너무 무서워서 그 자리에서 꼼짝달싹 못 하고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that I stood there frozen, unable to move.

explain: '꼼짝'을 더 세게 말한 형태로, '꼼짝달싹 못 하다'처럼 거의 굳어진 표현으로 써요. 짧게 '꼼짝 못 하다'라고도 해요. '아내에게 꼼짝 못 하다'처럼 사람 뒤에 '에게'를 붙이면 상대에게 눌려 지낸다는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.example: 감기에 걸려서 하루 종일 꼼짝 못 했어요.
phrases.en: I had a cold, so I couldn't move all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼼짝달싹'보다 짧고 자주 쓰는 말로, 움직일 수 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter, more common form of 꼼짝달싹 못 하다, meaning you can't move.

phrases.example: 고양이가 소파 위에서 꼼짝달싹도 안 해요.
phrases.en: The cat doesn't move at all on the sofa.
phrases.nuance_ko: '못 하다' 대신 '안 하다'를 쓰면 움직일 수 있는데 일부러 안 움직인다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 안 하다 instead of 못 하다, it means someone could move but doesn't.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 아내에게 꼼짝 못 해요.
phrases.en: He is completely under his wife's thumb.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 뒤에 '에게'를 붙이면 몸이 아니라 그 사람에게 눌려 지낸다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에게 after a person means being dominated by them, not physically stuck.

explain_en: It is a stronger version of '꼼짝' and is used almost as a fixed expression, '꼼짝달싹 못 하다'. The shorter '꼼짝 못 하다' is also common. With a person plus '에게', as in '아내에게 꼼짝 못 하다', it means being dominated by that person.

examples.en: A knife becomes hard through tempering.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌을 앞두고 선수들이 혹독한 담금질에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Ahead of this season, the players started harsh, toughening training.

examples.ko: 어려운 시기가 오히려 저에게 담금질이 됐어요.
examples.en: The hard times actually toughened me up.

examples.ko: 담금질 과정에서 열을 잘 조절해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to control the heat well during the tempering process.
That time was a tempering of my heart.
The coach made the team strong through rigorous training.

explain: 원래는 뜨겁게 달군 쇠를 물에 넣어 단단하게 하는 일인데, 힘든 훈련이나 경험으로 사람을 단련한다는 비유로도 많이 써요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '담금질에 들어가다'라는 표현을 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 대장장이가 칼을 불에 달궈 담금질을 해요.
phrases.en: The blacksmith heats the knife in the fire and tempers it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 담금질을 동작으로 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing for expressing it as an action.

phrases.example: 팀이 새 시즌을 위한 담금질에 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: The team has started intense training for the new season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠 뉴스에서 훈련을 시작한다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in sports news to mean starting training.

phrases.en: Steady training is needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이지만 담금질보다 힘든 과정이라는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but with less sense of a harsh process.

explain_en: Originally it is the process of heating metal and plunging it into water to harden it, but it is also widely used figuratively for toughening a person through hard training or experience. In sports news you often see the expression '담금질에 들어가다'.

examples.en: The father gave the child a shoulder ride.

examples.ko: 축제에서 아들을 목말 태우고 공연을 봤어요.
examples.en: At the festival I put my son on my shoulders and watched the show.
The child climbed onto Dad's shoulders and loves it.
Maybe the shoulder ride was comfortable, because the child fell asleep right away.
If you give a shoulder ride for long, your neck hurts.
My daughter begged to be carried on my shoulders.

explain: 어른이 아이를 어깨에 올릴 때는 '목말을 태우다', 아이가 올라탈 때는 '목말을 타다'로 짝을 맞춰 써요. 아이 키가 커서 구경하기 좋아지는 장면에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 아빠가 키가 작은 동생에게 목말을 태워 줬어요.
phrases.en: Dad gave my short little sibling a ride on his shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 아이를 어깨에 올릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an adult lifts a child onto their shoulders.

phrases.en: The child watched the fireworks riding on someone's shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이가 어른 어깨에 올라탈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a child climbs onto an adult's shoulders.

phrases.en: Dad, please give me a shoulder ride too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이가 부탁할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The way a child would ask for it.
phrases.en_equiv: please give me a shoulder ride

explain_en: The adult says '목말을 태우다' (give a shoulder ride) and the child says '목말을 타다' (ride on shoulders). It often appears when a child is lifted to see over a crowd.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 연기 방출을 줄이는 노력을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: This factory is working to reduce smoke emissions.

examples.ko: 난로는 열 방출이 빨라서 방이 금방 따뜻해져요.
examples.en: The heater gives off heat quickly, so the room warms up soon.
The club decided to release the underperforming player.
People evacuated because of a gas release accident.
Sweat helps the body release heat.
Emission standards got stricter, so factories are worried.

explain: 방출은 열·가스·에너지가 밖으로 나가는 일에 쓰고, 스포츠에서는 팀이 선수를 내보내는 일에도 써요. 비슷한 '배출'은 쓰레기·물·가스를 내보낼 때 쓰고, 방출은 열·빛·에너지처럼 퍼져 나가는 것에 어울려요. 뉴스에서 '선수 방출'이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: We have to stop the gas release.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가스가 밖으로 나가는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to gas escaping outward.

phrases.en: The factory's emission amount has gone down a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나가는 양이 얼마인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how much is released.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 이번에 선수 방출을 결정했어요.
phrases.en: That team decided to release players this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀이 선수를 내보내는 일에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when a team lets players go.

explain_en: Physical emission, or club or company letting something go. 방출 is heat, gas or energy going out, and in sports it means a team letting a player go. The similar '배출' fits waste, water and gas, while 방출 suits things that spread out like heat, light and energy. '선수 방출' is a common news phrase.

t90.ax: Sweat helps the body release heat.
